products.name: Notion Q&A
products.note: Knowledge base AI Q&A; workspace corpus access; permission-aware but broad exposure risk

reading.body:
Notion Labs embeds AI into its workspace platform as a paid add-on, positioning the product as a context-aware assistant that operates within a user's own data rather than a standalone interface.

Notion AI and Notion Q&A both draw on a user's workspace corpus, which means their utility depends on the volume and organization of data already stored in Notion. This is structurally different from general-purpose LLMs that operate on training data alone. The permission-aware design of Q&A attempts to respect access controls, though the data notes broad exposure risk, suggesting the product surfaces information more liberally than individual permission boundaries might warrant. This matters because it creates a scaling dynamic tied to workspace adoption: the more data users store in Notion, the more valuable the AI layer becomes, and the more compute Notion must provision per user.

Custom Agents introduce autonomous task execution on a credit system. This shifts Notion from chat interface toward workflow automation, which increases compute demand per user and per organization. The credit pricing model creates a variable cost structure unlike flat-rate AI features, meaning power consumption scales with usage intensity rather than seat count alone.

The data shows California law exposure but no recorded cases. It does not cover Notion's infrastructure location, power consumption, data center arrangements, or the LLM providers powering these features. It also does not address the total compute footprint of running inference on workspace-scale datasets, which would be necessary to understand how this product affects grid demand.

profile_text.body:
Notion Labs is a for-profit startup founded in 2013 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. The company produces Notion, a workspace platform, and describes it as one tool for search, generation, analysis, and chat. Its site positions the product as an all-in-one environment where users can work across pages, documents, tasks, and databases without switching between applications.

Notion AI is the company's embedded AI layer, included with Business and Enterprise plans. It draws on context from a user's workspace and connected applications such as Slack and Google Drive. Tracked products include Notion AI, described as a chat and general LLM feature embedded in the workspace, and Notion Q&A, a knowledge base question-and-answer tool with permission-aware but broad exposure risk noted in the held facts. Additional features described on the site include AI Meeting Notes for transcription and summarization, Enterprise Search with Notion AI Connectors, and Custom Agents that can run on schedules or triggers to handle multi-step tasks autonomously. Custom Agents operate on a credit system available as a Business and Enterprise add-on, priced at $10 per 1,000 credits. The site states that Notion AI enables HIPAA compliance through LLM provider zero-retention APIs, and that customer data is not used to train models unless users opt in, with contractual prohibitions in place for AI subprocessors as well.

The held facts show Notion Labs has 175 law exposure entries associated with California, though no specific litigation cases are recorded in the dataset. The company has a profile page on theworldofai.org and no MCP server presence noted.
